Create Labels for Fractional Data

Source: R/geom.R
geom_fraction_label.Rd

Adds labels to plots at specified fractional intervals. Labels can be positioned using either static values or functions for both x and y coordinates.

Usage

geom_fraction_label(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  position = "identity",
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  xpos = mean,
  ypos = 0,
  period = 5,
  initial = 0L,
  inherit.aes = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

mapping

Set of aesthetic mappings created by aes.

data

The data to be displayed in this layer.

position

Position adjustment, either as a string, or the result of a call to a position adjustment function. Default is "identity".

na.rm

If FALSE, the default, missing values are removed with a warning.

show.legend

logical. Should this layer be included in the legends?

xpos

Function or static value determining x position of labels. Default is mean.

ypos

Function or static value determining y position of labels. Default is 0.

period

Integer specifying the interval between labels. Default is 5.

initial

Integer specifying the starting point for fraction counting. Default is 0.

inherit.aes

If FALSE, overrides the default aesthetics.

...

Other arguments passed to layer.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Basic usage with default positioning
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y, fraction = frac)) +
  geom_fraction_label()

# Custom positioning using functions
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y, fraction = frac)) +
  geom_fraction_label(xpos = mean, ypos = max)
} # }
